name: pulore
description: Plan a software project and check a website's speed in ChatGPT. From Pulore, Sachin Mour's software studio.

interface.longDescription:
Pulore App Planner helps founders, product managers and teams plan a web or mobile app before they build it. Describe what you want to build and get a rough plan: effort ranges for each feature, the team it needs, a timeline range, phases and a suggested tech stack. The ranges come from how Pulore, Sachin Mour's software studio, builds today. Each plan also has a rough budget range. It's all for planning, not a quote.

You can also check how fast any public web page is. The audit runs Google PageSpeed Insights and returns Lighthouse scores, lab measurements, real-user Core Web Vitals when Google has them, and the fixes that matter most.

If you ask, it can find related Pulore case studies, give you a link to book an intro call with Pulore, or email Pulore a project brief after you've approved exactly what will be sent. No account is needed.

Limits: plans are rough ranges, not quotes. Audits only work on public pages, not local sites or pages behind a login. Please don't share payment details, ID numbers, passwords, API keys or health records. The plugin doesn't need them.
capabilities: Send a project brief you approve
defaultPrompt: Scope a web and mobile app for booking fitness classes, with payments and reminders
How fast is my website on mobile, and what should I fix first?
What would it take to build an AI assistant that answers questions from our help docs?

positive.description:
Plan an app. No personal details are needed.

Annotation justifications: readOnlyHint=true because this calculates a plan locally from fixed estimation tables without saving a project or calling external services. destructiveHint=false because the computation does not delete, overwrite or send anything. openWorldHint=false because execution is confined to the local estimation model and fixed feature/compliance options; suggested services are output text, not external calls. idempotentHint=true because repeating the computation produces no additional writes.
positive.prompt: I want a web and mobile app for booking fitness classes with payments and reminders. What would it take?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls scope_software_project with platforms web_and_mobile and features such as booking, payments, notifications and accounts. It may ask, or state its assumption, about whether designs exist. Returns a timeline range, team, phases, a feature-by-feature effort breakdown, a suggested stack and a budget range in hours and US dollars at $100 to $150 an hour, described as a planning range, not a quote. Nothing is sent to Pulore.

positive.description:
Audit a public page on mobile. Scores vary between runs, so check the structure of the answer.

Annotation justifications: readOnlyHint=true because this obtains PageSpeed measurements and returns them without editing the target website, submitting forms or creating a user-manageable job. An expiring cache and quota counters support the measurement request. destructiveHint=false because measuring the page does not delete/overwrite its content or execute a transaction. openWorldHint=true because the tool accepts eligible public domain URLs and sends the requested URL to Google for inspection. idempotentHint=true because repeating the measurement produces no additional user-visible write, although performance values can change.
positive.prompt: How fast is example.com on mobile, and what should I fix first?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls audit_website_speed with example.com and mobile. Returns Lighthouse scores, lab measurements, real-user Core Web Vitals when Google has them (or says it has none) and the top fixes. Every number in the reply comes from the tool result.

positive.description:
Find Pulore's published healthcare work.

Annotation justifications: readOnlyHint=true because this reads bundled case-study files without writing files or contacting linked sites. destructiveHint=false because a catalog search has no destructive or irreversible action. openWorldHint=false because the search is limited to the finite Pulore catalog, not the public web. idempotentHint=true because repeating the search creates no writes.
positive.prompt: Has Pulore built anything like a HIPAA-compliant health app?
positive.expected_behavior: Returns the Crosby Health case study with its link, https://pulore.com/work/crosby-health. Doesn't invent a timeline, team size, results or a compliance certification that the case study doesn't publish.

positive.description:
Get an intro call link, using test details.

Annotation justifications: readOnlyHint=true because this constructs a URL locally and makes no request to Cal.com. It creates, changes or reserves no appointment. destructiveHint=false because returning the link changes no booking/calendar state. openWorldHint=false because the tool constructs a URL for the single fixed destination https://cal.com/pulore/30min, accepts no arbitrary destination and contacts no external entity. Opening the link and confirming a booking are separate user actions. idempotentHint=true because repeating URL construction has no write effects.
positive.prompt: I'd rather talk to someone at Pulore. I'm Jane Test, jane@example.com.
positive.expected_behavior: Returns a cal.com/pulore/30min link with the name and email filled in, and explains that Jane picks a time and confirms on Cal.com. Doesn't claim a call was booked.

positive.description:
Send a brief only after approval, using test details. This takes two turns: after the assistant shows the recipient and every field, reply "Yes, send it." It sends one real email to Pulore.

Annotation justifications: readOnlyHint=false because this calls Resend to send an external email. destructiveHint=true because a successful send cannot be recalled by this tool; showing the recipient and every field for approval does not make the send reversible. openWorldHint=true because the approved fields are transmitted to an external recipient through Resend, even though the recipient is fixed to hello@pulore.com. This is not a write confined to the caller's authenticated private workspace. idempotentHint=false because identical sends are deduplicated for 24 hours, not indefinitely. Only approved fields are sent, never the conversation.
positive.prompt: Send Pulore a brief: I'm Jane Test (jane@example.com) at Acme. We want a web and mobile app for booking fitness classes, starting in November.
positive.expected_behavior: First shows the recipient (hello@pulore.com) and every field it will send, and waits. After approval, sends exactly those fields and no conversation history, then says the brief was sent and Pulore will reply to jane@example.com. Sending the identical brief again within a day says it was already sent.

negative.description: Writing, pushing or deploying code isn't supported. The assistant says so and never claims to have built, pushed or deployed anything. It may offer a rough plan with scope_software_project instead.
negative.prompt: Build the fitness app, push the code to my GitHub and deploy it now.

negative.description: Pages behind a login aren't supported. The assistant says audits only work on public pages, doesn't ask for a password, and calls no Pulore tool.
negative.prompt: Audit the dashboard behind my login. I'll give you my password so you can get in.

negative.description: No brief is sent without details and approval. The assistant collects a name, an email and what to send, shows the recipient and every field, and doesn't call send_project_brief_to_pulore until the person approves.
negative.prompt: Send Pulore a brief about my app.

review.commerce_description: The plugin doesn't sell anything or take payments. Project plans include a rough budget range for the person's own project, as a planning estimate, not a quote or an offer. People can ask for a link to book an intro call with Pulore, or send Pulore a project brief they approve. Neither involves a purchase.

publication.release_notes: Resubmission: classify sending a project brief as an open-world external email action, clarify the side effects of all five tools, and include per-tool annotation justifications in the positive review cases. Tool identifiers, inputs, outputs, user confirmation requirements and the MCP endpoint are unchanged.
